reasoning:
The user wants me to design a weight-storage format similar to FTW (Fast Transformer Weights, presumably — there's a paper "FTW: Fast Transformer Weights" or similar; actually FTW is "Fast Weight Loading" — I recall a recent paper about fast LLM weight loading from disk, e.g., "FTW" by some authors that pre-merges MoE experts into flattened banks and uses direct I/O). The design requirements:

1. Experts pre-merged into flattened (layer*E+e) banks — i.e., for MoE models with E experts per layer, instead of storing experts grouped per layer with an indirection, we flatten the expert index across layers so the file layout is one contiguous bank per (layer, expert) pair, ordered by global index g = layer*E + e. This makes reads large and contiguous.

2. Read with parallel direct I/O into final host layout — use O_DIRECT reads (bypass page cache), multiple threads/queues issuing reads in parallel, reading directly into the pinned host buffers at their final addresses (no extra copy/staging).

3. Pinned after fill — allocate host memory as pageable first? Actually "pinned after fill" suggests: allocate normal pageable memory, issue direct I/O directly into it (direct I/O can write into any user buffer regardless of pinning since DMA happens synchronously during read syscall... well, on Linux, O_DIRECT read into a user buffer will pin the pages for the duration of the I/O internally via get_user_pages), then after all data is loaded, call mlock to pin it. This avoids needing huge pinned allocations upfront (which can fail or cause memory pressure), avoids warmup (no need to touch pages / no cudaHostRegister cost?), and the weights are ready immediately.

Actually let me think about what FTW is. There's a 2024/2025 paper: "FTW: Fast Weight Loading for MoE models"? Hmm. I recall "Fast Inference of Mixture-of-Experts Language Models with Offloading" (Mixtral offloading), "LLM in a flash" (Apple), PowerInfer, llama.cpp mmap. And there's a recent paper about loading HuggingFace checkpoints fast using parallel direct IO and thread pools — maybe "FTW" = "Faster Than Words"? Not sure. The prompt says "(like FTW)" so they just want something in that spirit. I'll design my own format.

Key design elements:

**File format:**

- Header/magic, version, model metadata: dtype, num_layers L, experts per layer E, hidden dims, shapes of each tensor kind.
- Tensor kinds: attention (q,k,v,o), MLP w1/w3 (gate/up), w2 (down), plus shared/dense parts (embeddings, norms, lm_head, dense layers if hybrid).
- Expert tensors stored as banks indexed by g = layer*E + e, contiguous within bank, aligned.
- Non-expert ("dense") tensors stored separately, also aligned, possibly interleaved so they load early.
- Alignment: every region 4 KiB aligned (or larger, e.g., 2 MiB for huge pages / NVMe optimal); offsets stored in a table.
- Optionally store tensors already in the exact byte layout the runtime expects (e.g., transposed, padded, quantized blocks) so no post-processing.
- Checksums per bank (optional, cheap CRC of header only; full checksum optional flag).
- Extents table: array of {offset, nbytes} per tensor id, tensor id = f(kind, layer, expert).

**Layout ordering:** Order banks so that reads are big sequential streams per file, and so that the load order matches the order needed... but requirement says "no warmup" and "pinned after fill", meaning we load everything before serving, so ordering matters mainly for bandwidth saturation, not for time-to-first-token. Still, we might want dense/shared weights first so that once loading completes everything is there anyway. Since it's full load then serve, ordering is about maximizing throughput: many large contiguous reads across multiple files (shards).

**Load path:**

1. Open shard files with O_DIRECT (and O_NOATIME). Fall back to buffered if O_DIRECT unsupported (alignment issues).
2. Allocate destination buffers with plain malloc/mmap (pageable) sized exactly to final layout — the "final host layout": e.g., per-layer structs with pointers, or one big arena with pointer table. Direct I/O requires sector-aligned offsets and lengths and ideally aligned buffers; to read directly into arbitrary final addresses, either:
   - Make the final layout itself aligned: place each tensor at 512B/4KiB-aligned offsets within an arena allocated page-aligned (mmap), so each read target is aligned; pad inter-tensor gaps.
   - Or use bounce buffers per thread (aligned, e.g., 1–2 MiB) and memcpy — but requirement says "read ... into final host layout", i.e., direct placement, no bounce copy. So enforce alignment in the format: every tensor's file offset ≡ its host offset mod 4096, and sizes padded to 4 KiB multiples (padding bytes ignored).
3. Thread pool: N workers (N = number of queues/cores, tune 8–32), each pulls (fd, file_offset, dst_ptr, nbytes) chunks from an atomic work queue. Chunks are big (e.g., 256 KiB–4 MiB, or whole banks split into ~1–2 MiB pieces) to amortize syscalls; pread64 with O_DIRECT. Alternatively io_uring with registered... but registering pinned buffers conflicts with "pinned after fill". With io_uring you can do O_DIRECT reads into non-pinned buffers fine (kernel pins during I/O). But simple pread threads are portable and saturate NVMe easily. Could mention both: default pread worker pool; optional io_uring SQPOLL for higher QD.
4. After all chunks complete: verify sizes, optionally checksum, then mlock() the arena(s) (pin after fill), optionally madvise(MADV_WILLNEED) not needed since already resident; touch not needed because direct I/O already populated pages and they're resident (they were just written). Then build pointer tables / hand to runtime. No warmup pass needed because pages are resident and TLBs will populate naturally; optionally a single-touch pass if paranoid, but requirement says no warmup — direct I/O writes make pages present and dirty-resident; mlock keeps them.
5. GPU path (if relevant): after host fill + pin, register with CUDA (cudaHostRegister) or just cudaMemcpyAsync H2D per device with pinned staging... The question focuses on host layout though. Keep it host-centric, mention optional device upload.

**Why these choices:**

- Flattened (layer*E+e): turns E*L small per-expert tensors into L*E contiguous banks per tensor-kind; each bank is a single large extent → few, large, sequential direct reads; no indirection/gather at load; also enables streaming any subset (expert subsets for routing-aware partial loads later).
- Parallel direct I/O: bypasses page cache (avoids double-copy and cache pollution, avoids dirty page writeback stealing bandwidth), scales QD across NVMe channels, avoids mmap/page-fault serialization storms.
- Pinned after fill: allocating GBs of pinned (page-locked) memory up front often fails due to overcommit limits (vm.max_map_count? no—locked limit) and stresses the kernel; filling into pageable memory via O_DIRECT works because the kernel takes page refs during the syscall; afterwards mlock pins them now that content is resident — mlock on already-populated ranges doesn't need to fault anything in, it's fast. No warmup: pages are already resident from the DIO writes; no first-touch faults remain (well, the pages are present; PTEs exist because kernel wrote through them... actually with O_DIRECT the kernel does GUP and copies into struct pages; the user PTEs are already mapped (from mmap/malloc fault-in at allocation? malloc via mmap gives lazy zero pages!). Hmm — careful: if we mmap anonymous memory, pages aren't faulted until touched. O_DIRECT read into an untouched anonymous page: the kernel's GUP will fault the page in (it handles this — get_user_pages triggers faulting for anonymous memory). So after DIO, pages are allocated and resident. Good — no warmup needed. If we used MAP_POPULATE at allocation, even better determinism but that's basically pre-faulting, cheap relative to disk read anyway.)

Edge considerations:

- Alignment contract: FS block size (usually 4096); st_blksize; logical block size of device (512 or 4096; some NVMe support larger). Format guarantees: superblock 4KiB; each tensor region offset 4KiB-aligned; logical size padded to 4KiB; logical size recorded separately from padded size.
- Host arena: mmap with MAP_NORESERVE|MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_ANONYMOUS, base 4KiB-aligned naturally; map tensor i to arena_offset_i such that (dst - base) % 4096 == (file_off % 4096) == 0. Simplest: both sides 4KiB-aligned always.
- Chunking: split each bank into chunks of CHUNK=1–2 MiB (multiple of 4KiB), push (fd, off, ptr, len) jobs; workers loop atomic fetch_add on job index. Per-thread local buffer not needed. Use pread64. Handle short reads by looping.
- NUMA: interleave arena across nodes or bind loader threads round-robin; for inference single-node usually fine; mention numa_alloc_interleaved option.
- Hugepages: could back arena with THP (madvise MADV_HUGEPAGE) after fill to reduce TLB pressure; alignment of tensors to 2MiB optional mode for that. Mention as variant: ALIGN=2MiB mode where each bank is 2MiB-aligned enabling THP and avoiding splits.
- Sharding: split banks across S shard files so parallelism spans devices/controllers; round-robin banks to shards, keep each bank contiguous within a shard (never split a bank across shards to preserve sequentiality per file... or allow stripe width = chunk across shards for RAID0-like behavior; simpler: distribute whole banks round-robin).
- Metadata: JSON or binary TOC. Binary TOC fixed-size records for simplicity; include dtype enum, shape tuple, quantization format id, scale-offset pointers (for block-quantized formats like FP4/INT4 with group scales — store scales adjacent to blocks inside same bank so one read gets both).
- Integrity: xxh3/CRC32C per bank stored in TOC; verification optional post-load (parallel too) — but adds time; make it a flag. At minimum magic+version+TOC checksum.
- Endianness/dtype conversion: none — format stores native runtime dtype (the "pre-baked" idea: convert once at packaging time; loader is pure copy). That's key to "read into final layout": bytes on disk are byte-identical to what runtime consumes.
- Final host layout definition: define struct-of-arrays vs array-of-structs. For inference, typical: per-layer contiguous blocks: [attn weights][mlp expert banks]. Provide `Layout` descriptor generated by packager: list of regions with (tensor_id, file_off, host_off, nbytes). Runtime allocates one arena of total_bytes, and after load computes pointers = base + host_off. Also provide convenience: the TOC's host_off equals file_off minus dense_region_start etc. Simplest invariant: host_off == file_off - DATA_START, i.e., the data section is a byte-for-byte image of the host arena! That's elegant: the entire payload section is exactly the memory image; loader = copy file→arena. Then "final host layout" is trivially defined by the file. Dense/shared tensors placed first (layers 0..L interleaved?) Hmm, but ordering for bandwidth: with full parallel load of everything, order barely matters. Keep invariant host_off = file_off − PAYLOAD_BASE. Padding gaps between tensors allowed (reserved=0xFF or zeros).

Wait — but should non-expert weights be in the same image? Yes: embeddings, norms, lm_head, dense-layer weights all live in the same payload image at fixed offsets. Expert banks occupy the bulk.

- Multi-file: payload striped across shards; then host_off mapping needs per-shard base. Alternative: keep single-file-per-shard where each shard covers a contiguous slice of the global address space (like a sparse image split at bank boundaries). I.e., partition the set of banks (plus dense tensors) into S groups; shard s contains those regions packed contiguously; TOC has global host_off per tensor plus shard_id and shard_off. Loader opens all shards, jobs reference (shard_fd, shard_off, base+host_off, len). Invariant relaxed but still no bounce buffers.

- Loading steps enumerated precisely with syscalls.

- Failure handling: short read/EIO retry policy, fallback to buffered IO path (drop O_DIRECT, use page cache + read) automatically when alignment fails (e.g., tmpfs, network FS).

- Concurrency numbers: QD total = threads × 1 (pread) ; aim QD 16–64. Chunk 1MiB ⇒ for 100GB, 100k jobs — fine. Or chunk 4MiB ⇒ 25k jobs.

- Also mention fallocate/extent hints: packager writes sequentially with O_DIRECT too, ensuring extents are contiguous-ish (fallocate to preallocate, reducing fragmentation → better read sequentiality).

- Security/integrity: version field, feature flags, dtype registry.

Loader pseudocode:

```c
void* load(const char* dir, Layout* out){
  int fd[S]; open shards O_RDONLY|O_DIRECT|O_NOATIME;
  hdr = read+validate header & TOC (buffered small reads ok, or DIO into stack buf);
  void* base = mmap(0, hdr.arena_bytes, PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE,
                    MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_ANONYMOUS|MAP_NORESERVE);
  madvise(base, bytes, MADV_NOHUGEPAGE);
  // build jobs
  Job* jobs; int nj=0;
  for t in TOC:
    for (u64 o=0; o<t.padbytes; o+=CHUNK)
      jobs[nj++]={fd[t.shard], t.file_off+o, base+t.host_off+o, min(CHUNK,t.padbytes-o)};
  sort jobs by (shard, file_off);
  atomic next=0; failures=0;
  spawn T workers bound round-robin across NUMA nodes:
    while((i=fetch_add(&next,1))<nj){ j=jobs[i]; u64 done=0;
      while(done<j.len){ ssize_t r=pread64(j.fd,(char*)j.dst+done,j.len-done,j.off+done);
```
